431:
He can draw a ten-ruble note
in half an hour that looks completely real!
432:
- Is that him?
- Damned if I know. I'll check.
433:
- Excuse me, do you have a match?
- I don't smoke.
434:
- Well? - No, not him.
- A cop. - Definitely.
435:
We checked the Docent's accomplices'
addresses. The helmet isn't there.
436:
That leaves one possibility:
the cloakroom attendant, Prokhorov.
437:
But we haven't been able to check it.
Prokhorov didn't come to the meeting.
438:
He probably suspected something.
He quit his job and hasn't been home.
440:
I owe you a thousand apologies
and a tremendous thank-you.
Take off the wig, wash off the tattoos,
441:
go home and celebrate New Year.
Thank you very much.
- What about my men?
442:
We'll return your charges
to prison today.
443:
If the cloakroom attendant turns up,
might you need us again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you,
but Bely—the real Docent—
escaped from prison today.
445:
Unbelievable, but true.
It's dangerous for you to stay in disguise.
446:
Could it wait until tomorrow?
It is New Year, and they have tried
in their own way.
447:
We're outside the city.
Docent is unlikely to find us.
448:
All right, but don't set foot off the dacha grounds!
We forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife.
Here's her reply, addressed to him.
450:
- You'll have lunch with us on the first?
- We promise!
451:
It's a shame. Such a nice woman,
and her father's a fence and a profiteer.
452:
What's all this shouting?
Who said you could go out?
- There he is... Bad person.
454:
The New Year is here.
I wish you all a fresh start this year.
455:
Anything can happen, but remember:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll be sure to find you.
457:
- And now... just a moment...
- Where's he going?
458:
Who knows? You can't make sense
of anything he says anymore.
459:
What's to make sense of?
He says he'll find us anywhere
and slit our throats.
461:
They say he went snick! across Ryaby's throat
with a razor. That was that.
- He's gone completely savage, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to see you?
Father Frost, bringing presents!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What have I done?
- Come on. Wear these in good health.
They're slippers.
464:
- What do I need them for?
I don't even have a home.
- You will. There's time yet.
465:
- Meanwhile, they'll come in handy in prison.
- Always predicting doom.
466:
These are for you, Vasya...
And these are yours, Gavrila Petrovich.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you, too.
469: Sour stuff. It's dull without vodka.
470:
- Do we have to get drunk as pigs?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could sit and have
a heart-to-heart talk.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor.
I don't do heart-to-hearts with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Listen to him! Think I'd be a sucker
and play cards with you?
You've got nine aces in that deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow,"
476:
and you name a city starting
with its last letter, W: Warsaw.
Then you say one starting with W. Got it?
477: Your turn, Fedya. Name one starting with W.
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I was locked up there.
479:
- All right. Now yours has to start with A.
- Dzhambul. - Where did Dzhambul come from?
480:
It's warm there.
My home is there. My mother.
481:
Let's try something else.
I'll go out, you'll hide something,
then I'll come back and find it.
482:
- You'd do better to find our helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We'll hide it, and he'll peek through a hole?
- Why would I? You can go out and hide it.
484:
You watch me to make sure I don't peek.
Why me? It's always Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your mouth open, you little rascal!
- Mouth, mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever a little boy?
- I was.
487:
- Did you have a mother and father?
- I did.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Why are you like a dog?
490:
- Came on his own.
- Oh, you're here too.
491:
I tried your place,
but I could tell it was staked out.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Keep walking.
495:
- Sorry we bothered you for nothing, Doctor.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him valerian, some warm tea,
and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Dear Dad, we found out
that you're in prison,
500:
and we're very happy,
because we thought you were dead."
501:
What bastard told that little kid
his father's in prison?
502:
"Mom was happy too, because when
your letter came, she cried all day.
503:
She used to tell me
you were a test pilot."
505:
"But I'm glad you're alive anyway,
because Mom says
507:
That's right! Weak-willed enough
to steal our money and blame the taxi driver.
508: Scram! I'll knock your horns off, radish!
510:
You should be ashamed!
You're forty years old.
Half your life is behind you.
511:
What's in your past? Your present?
What lies ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses before it's too late.
That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we need to get out.
The doctor will tell the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I took a razor to her throat...
515:
She's lying in the well.
Go and look.
516: What did I start with? One year.
517: How many for the escape? Three!
518:
How many for the kindergarten
and the apartment? Say ten!
520:
And I'm supposed to put up with
that snake for a lousy fourteen years?
521:
The one who put the old woman in the well?
Do what you like. I'm going to the police.
522: Go on! He won't hurt you.
523:
What about you?
Will you keep putting up with him
until he kills you?
524:
Vasya, I told him earlier I had a cold,
and he just...
525:
Enough about your cold already.
Come here...
527:
- What are you doing?
- Cleaning the carpet.
528:
Well, comrades, the show's over.
First, I'll take this off.
530:
Once I've served my sentence, that's it.
I'm going straight! I'll get a job.
531:
- Doing what? Watchman at my village collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I could shovel snow, lay bricks,
or be a translator. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the hat!
Who is Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are lots of crooks,
but only one hat.
- The helmet might get our sentences reduced.
535:
Where did he put it?
We went everywhere.
536:
Crook! I told you I had a cold,
and all you said was,
"I'll rip your mouth open!"
537:
- Tried to make me dive in that cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us.
Remember? He said he was fishing
and told me to dive.
539:
- Wait. What did he say about fishing?
- He was fishing through a hole in the ice,
540:
- and asked, "Kosoy, can you swim?"
- He hid the helmet in that hole!
541:
That's it! I remember, the radish!
It's in the ice hole at Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you lout?
You could've left a note when you hanged yourself.
- Let's go.
543:
- What about him?
- Let them come get him.
I'm not carrying that big ox. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing down there.
- There is, on the bottom.
Someone has to dive.
546:
Why me? Every little thing is Kosoy's job.
Vasya, tell him to dive himself.
547: I can't! It's cold. I'll get sick.
548:
- Just now he was hanging himself,
and now he's afraid of catching cold!
- Sporting greetings!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I'd kill you both if I had the time!
552:
Now there are two of him.
And there's another at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich! Well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
